A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PerceptionLM work. Their main text, tables, figures, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original PLM benchmark evaluations, synthetic-data scaling experiments, and data ablations, including supplementary results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a HardQA comparison and evaluations against LLaMA-3V.

M1.justification: The PE/Llama architecture, MLP projector, tiling and pooling, three-stage training procedure, and annotation engines remain unchanged. Revised training settings and newly disclosed filtering practices do not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Training sources and task coverage remain substantively unchanged, including all five PLM-VideoBench tasks. The new comparisons reuse existing image and HardQA benchmarks. Despite removed score columns, Appendix C still describes VATEX, How2QA, TVQA, and TVBench evaluations, while MME remains discussed in the limitations.

E2.justification: v2 adds LLaMA 3.2V-11B and 90B comparisons in Table 12. Tables 3 and 4 remove Gemma 3-4B/12B, InternVL2-1B/4B/8B, and Qwen2VL-7B; the relocated image-captioning comparison also omits the older InternVL2 and Qwen2VL-7B rows. Some removed comparators remain in other experiments, but membership changes substantially within these comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix A.1 changes the reported warm-up batch size from 64 to 512, stage-2 training size from 64M to 72.5M, and stage-3 size from 21M to 19.1M. Corresponding mixture tables revise numerous source allocations, and the scaling setup changes its stated synthetic/human sample counts. These are substantial reported setting revisions; neither PDF establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Figure 7 adds a targeted PLM-data ablation on the seven-benchmark HardQA aggregate, reporting 39.6 without PLM data and 45.6 with the full mix. The existing Table 6 ablations, encoder/input scaling analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and scaling curves without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added comparisons introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds LLaMA-3V results and the HardQA ablation, while removing MME, VATEX, How2QA, TVQA, and TVBench score columns and numerous comparator entries. Retained benchmark, grounding, long-video, and Table 6 entries largely preserve their numbers; image-captioning scores are relocated. New Table 12 reports PLM-8B ChartQA as 86.5, conflicting with 85.5 in both versions' Table 3, rather than establishing a performance gain.

T1.justification: The empirical power-law expression, fitting rationale, and substantive metric definitions are retained. No theorem, proof, or new formal argument is introduced; revised token-count arithmetic concerns implementation documentation.

C1.justification: The open, reproducible PLM framework, human-annotated datasets, and PLM-VideoBench remain the central contributions. v2's introduction removes the explicit Qwen2.5-VL benchmark-win counts and associated state-of-the-art assertion, retaining the broader claim of competitive performance.

C2.justification: v2 Section 6.2 removes explicit attributions of hard-perception and grounding strengths to the pretrained PE encoder. New Appendix M discusses residual bias and harmful outputs despite filtering and refusal training. The existing long-video, base-LLM, SGQA, and data-scope limitations are retained in Appendix L.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially revises the documented training recipe and per-source sample accounting, including image-token counts that incorporate the existing thumbnail. Section 5 distinguishes STC captions from derived training instances, and Appendix M newly discloses filtering/refusal practices. The direct PLM dataset link is removed, while the code-repository reference remains. These documentation changes do not establish new resource availability or procedures.

R1.justification: The Gemma 3 technical-report citation is removed. The remaining cited works largely match after reference renumbering and metadata updates, and the positioning around open data and detailed video understanding remains substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses the introduction and explanatory passages, moves Related Work near the beginning, merges the human-data discussion, and makes PLM-VideoBench a subsection. It adds an appendix contents page, relocates limitations and qualitative results, and reorganizes supplementary results.

P2.justification: The document receives a different typographic layout and extensive table restructuring. Image-captioning results move into Table 13, Figure 7 and Table 12 are added, and the training-data overview is revised. Synthetic-data examples replace several link-only placeholders with embedded images or video frames.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful HardQA evidence, a comparison with the caption-generating model, clearer data explanations, and embedded examples. However, it removes substantial reported comparisons and introduces numerical inconsistencies: Section 5 states that 194.2K + 194.2K + 122.3K equals 522.7K rather than 510.7K, and Table 12 conflicts with Table 3 on ChartQA. These gains and reporting weaknesses, alongside largely retained core results, prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
